text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Saturday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
AL-RAI
- Islamic Action Front asks Moslem Brotherhood to ease pressure for immediate announcement of an election boycott so the front can hold discussions with other opposition political parties.

- Interior Minister Nazir Rasheed says government has no plans for an interim law targeting political parties and the professional unions. Says Moslem Brotherhood are a basic part of society. Says Jordan plans a ditch on its north-eastern borders to prevent smuggling.
- Military court will pass sentence today on Ahmed Daqamsa, the soldier who shot dead seven Israeli schoolgirls in March. Judicial sources do not expect the death sentence.
- Prime Minister Abdul-Salam al-Majali to visit Palestinian-ruled territories on Sunday for talks with President Yasser Arafat, Palestinians say.
AD-DUSTOUR
- Shell oil company has had promising results from tests of oil-bearing rocks in Jordan and will set up station to produce 5,000 barrels per day, possibly doubling output later.
- Islamic Action Front awaits results of its consultations with other opposition parties on possible boycott of parliamentary elections.
- Professional unions to issue detailed statement today calling for boycott of elections.
- Universities expected to raise fees to cut deficits.
- Tourism official says holiday bookings for second half of the year point to a promising tourist season.
- Foreign Minister Fayez al-Tarawnah says conditions not right for holding Arab summit now.
AL-ARAB AL-YAWM
- Leading figure in Moslem Brotherhood warns that a decision to boycott parliamentary elections could lead to a split in the movement and the establishment of a new Islamist party.
AL-ASWAQ
- Trade and Industry Minister Hani al-Mulqi says ministry will set up special unit to tackle difficulties faced by industrialists.
- Stock exchange chief says bourse monitoring committee will be appointed within days.
- Treasury made 31 million dinars ($44 million) in first six months of the year from selling and buying real estate.
JORDAN TIMES
- Jordan, Kuwait maintain contact on the road to reconciliation, Prime Minister Majali says.
- Government determined to ensure political parties adhere to the law, Interior Minister Rasheed says.
